# Data Acquisition & Cleaning
```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: false

library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(readxl)
library(fs)
library(gt)

load_netflix_data <- function(){
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
  
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    return(local)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |>
    mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
           path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
           data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
           data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |> 
    select(-clean_time) |> 
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |> 
    filter_out(Title == "") |> 
    rename(
      title = Title,
      runtime = Runtime,
      views = Views,
      hours_viewed = `Hours Viewed`,
      release_date = `Release Date`,
      available_globally = `Available Globally?`
    ) |>
    mutate(
      year = as.integer(year),
      available_globally = (available_globally == "Yes")
    ) |>
    select(year, period, period_start, period_end, title, runtime, views, 
           hours_viewed, release_date, available_globally, live_event)
}

NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data()
```

# Further Analysis & Tables 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-consistent-staples
#| tbl-cap: "Top Consistent 'Staple' Titles Across Multiple Periods"
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

NETFLIX_DATA |>
  group_by(title) |>
  summarize(
    appearances = n(),
    avg_hours = mean(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_hours = min(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_hours = sd(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  filter(appearances >= 5) |> 
  arrange(desc(min_hours)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(avg_hours, min_hours, sd_hours), decimals = 0) |>
  cols_label(
    title = "Title",
    appearances = "Periods Appeared",
    avg_hours = "Average Hours",
    min_hours = "Minimum Hours",
    sd_hours = "Std. Deviation"
  )
```

# Shows vs. Movies 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-shows-vs-movies
#| tbl-cap: "Fraction of Watch Time: Shows vs. Movies"
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

NETFLIX_DATA |>
  mutate(
    content_type = if_else(runtime > 240 | str_detect(title, "(?i)Season"), "TV Show", "Movie")
  ) |>
  group_by(period, content_type) |>
  summarize(total_hours = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(period) |>
  mutate(fraction = total_hours / sum(total_hours)) |>
  select(period, content_type, fraction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = content_type, values_from = fraction) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_percent(columns = c(`TV Show`, Movie), decimals = 1) |>
  cols_label(period = "Period")
```

# Live Events Vs. Pre-Recorded Content
```{r}
#| label: tbl-live-vs-taped
#| tbl-cap: "Performance Comparison: Live Events vs. Pre-Taped Content"
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

NETFLIX_DATA |>
  mutate(content_format = if_else(live_event, "Live Event", "Pre-Taped")) |>
  group_by(content_format) |>
  summarize(
    total_titles = n(),
    avg_hours = mean(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_hours = max(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(avg_hours, max_hours), decimals = 0) |>
  cols_label(
    content_format = "Format",
    total_titles = "Total Offerings",
    avg_hours = "Average Viewership (Hrs)",
    max_hours = "Top Tier Viewership (Hrs)"
  )
```

## Initial Data Exploration

```{r}
#| label: task4-eda-pass
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
library(skimr)

glimpse(NETFLIX_DATA)
skim(NETFLIX_DATA)
```




After completing the EDA pass using the glimpse() and skim() I can say that the cleaned up dataset consists of 61892 rows and has a 11 columns total. Each row has a unique category, such as year, period (period start/end), title, runtime, views, hours viewed, release date, global availability, and whether or not the content was a live event or pre-taped. All in all, the data pipeline for the Netlfix report was completed successfully. 

## Exploratory Questions & Summary Findings

```{r}
#| label: task5-inline-calcs
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(stringr)
library(scales)

min_date <- min(NETFLIX_DATA$period_start, na.rm = TRUE)
max_date <- max(NETFLIX_DATA$period_end, na.rm = TRUE)
num_unique_titles <- n_distinct(NETFLIX_DATA$title)

bridgerton_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(str_detect(title, "Bridgerton")) |>
  summarize(total = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(total)

stranger_things_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(str_detect(title, "Stranger Things")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(title, "Beyond Stranger Things")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(title, "Tales from")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(title, "Fireplace")) |>
  summarize(total = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(total)

top10_2026h1_share <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(period == "2026H1") |>
  mutate(total_period_hours = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  slice_max(hours_viewed, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  summarize(top10_share = sum(hours_viewed) / first(total_period_hours)) |>
  pull(top10_share)

global_by_title <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  summarize(frac = mean(available_globally, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(frac)

global_by_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  summarize(frac = sum(hours_viewed * available_globally, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(frac)
```
1. What date range is covered by this data set?
The Netflix engagement dataset covers the period from `r min(NETFLIX_DATA$period_start, na.rm = TRUE)` to `r max(NETFLIX_DATA$period_end, na.rm = TRUE)`.

2. How many different shows and movies are covered in this data set?
The dataset encompasses a total of `r scales::comma(num_unique_titles)` unique catalog titles.

3. How many total hours have been spent watching shows from the Bridgerton universe?
Shows from the *Bridgerton* universe generated a massive `r scales::comma(bridgerton_hours)` hours of total watch time.

4. How many total hours have been spent watching the five seasons of Stranger Things?
The five main seasons of *Stranger Things* (excluding companion content and spin-offs) accounted for `r scales::comma(stranger_things_hours)` hours viewed.

5. What percentage of total watch time was spent on the Top 10 titles of 2026H1?
The Top 10 titles of 2026H1 alone represented `r scales::percent(top10_2026h1_share, accuracy = 0.01)` of all viewership during that period.

6. What fraction of Netflix’s catalog is globally available? (Answered both by title and weighted by hours viewed)
Global catalog availability stands at `r scales::percent(global_by_title, accuracy = 0.1)` by total title count, which shifts to `r scales::percent(global_by_hours, accuracy = 0.1)` when weighted by total hours viewed.

# Platform Strategy Memo

```{r}
#| label: memo-supporting-calcs
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Supporting metrics for your 750-word memo (use these inline with `r ...` so nothing is hard-coded!)
tv_movie_summary <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  mutate(is_show = (!is.na(runtime) & runtime > 240) | str_detect(title, "(?i)Season")) |>
  summarize(
    tv_share = sum(hours_viewed[is_show], na.rm = TRUE) / sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    movie_share = sum(hours_viewed[!is_show], na.rm = TRUE) / sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
memo_tv_share <- percent(tv_movie_summary$tv_share, accuracy = 0.1)
memo_movie_share <- percent(tv_movie_summary$movie_share, accuracy = 0.1)

titles_2023h1 <- sum(NETFLIX_DATA$period == "2023H1")
titles_2026h1 <- sum(NETFLIX_DATA$period == "2026H1")
hours_2023h1 <- sum(NETFLIX_DATA$hours_viewed[NETFLIX_DATA$period == "2023H1"], na.rm = TRUE)
hours_2026h1 <- sum(NETFLIX_DATA$hours_viewed[NETFLIX_DATA$period == "2026H1"], na.rm = TRUE)

global_share_2023h1 <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(period == "2023H1") |>
  summarize(s = sum(hours_viewed * available_globally, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(s) |>
  percent(accuracy = 0.1)

global_share_2026h1 <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(period == "2026H1") |>
  summarize(s = sum(hours_viewed * available_globally, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(s) |>
  percent(accuracy = 0.1)

live_avg_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |> filter(live_event) |> summarize(m = mean(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) |> pull(m)
taped_avg_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |> filter(!live_event) |> summarize(m = mean(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) |> pull(m)
```
